scope: PR #183 (13 files): always-on/run-check.mjs (the fail-closed checker runner); test/run-check.test.mjs; the ADR skill SKILL.md + always-on/upstream-contributor-process.md pointing checkers at the runner; two features/always-on/*.feature + features/steps/checker-fail-closed.steps.mjs + datastore; ADR-0096; CHANGELOG; package.json. The reviewer traced every exit path of the runner and found NO path where a missing/failed/unstartable/timed-out checker reads as exit 0; arch-gate, links, routing, and the BDD chain passed.

boundary.evidence: a single shared front door for running any checker; resolution + fail-closed translation are centralized here instead of copied into each caller/hook (pattern-selector: a small command module, no new abstraction).

ownership.evidence: one owner of checker resolution and the exit-code contract (0 pass / 1 checker-failed / 2 block); no value written in two places.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins only (node:fs, node:child_process, node:crypto, node:path, node:url, node:os); the web-concern grep's only hits are the word 'Windows' matching /window/, no request/response/session/fetch.

error-handling.evidence: every path fails closed, traced by the reviewer: bad args/unsafe name/unsupported ext -> block before any fs access; skill-not-installed and checker-missing -> block naming the install path+command; ETIMEDOUT -> block (timeout, never a pass); status 0 only reachable after no error and no timeout. Hardened after review: signal-kill (status null) now its own explicit block; ENOBUFS its own block with maxBuffer raised to 10 MB so a verbose PASSING checker is not false-blocked; the inline statSync is wrapped (isFile) so a TOCTOU removal blocks cleanly; the identical-branch runnerArgs ternary removed.

boundary.evidence: integration tests spawning the real runner against sandboxed skills dirs.

error-handling.evidence: discriminating: against a no-op run-check (always exit 0), 15 of 16 tests fail (the one that still passes is the explicitly-labeled shell-pipe characterization, which never invokes run-check). Note-1 fix: added a signal-kill test (never reads as pass; exit 2 where the null-status branch fires on POSIX) and a verbose-passing-checker test (>1 MB output still passes, pinning the maxBuffer raise). 16 pass.

boundary.evidence: documentation: the ADR skill (the audit's proven failure) and the contributor process now run checkers through the runner, never by a folder-relative path and never through a tail/head pipe.

ownership.evidence: the run-through-the-runner convention is stated once in upstream-contributor-process.md for every checker; the ADR skill is the worked example.

error-handling.evidence: the guidance states the fail-closed contract and the pipefail fallback for when a pipe is unavoidable.

boundary.evidence: the three @audience:agent scenarios drive the real run-check.mjs: a missing skill, a missing checker, and a timed-out checker each BLOCK (exit 2).

ownership.evidence: step defs write only temp fixtures; no step-text collision with existing step files.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins; spawns the real runner.

error-handling.evidence: assertions throw on a wrong exit; a no-op runner flips all three 'does not continue / does not end' assertions. 18/18 scenarios pass on the harness.

boundary.evidence: ADR-0096 records the decision (runner + convention, not docs-only, not a full esk CLI) with options and honest limits; package.json wires test/run-check.test.mjs (guarded by all-tests-wired).

ownership.evidence: one ADR for the decision; the CHANGELOG entry is additive under 1.3.1.

error-handling.evidence: ADR names the limits: the runner reports a block but #174's Stop hook (which must itself exit 2, since hooks fail open) turns it into a stopped turn, under Claude Code's 8-continuation cap; a .sh checker needs bash and fails closed without it.

findings.finding: two fail-closed branches had no discriminating test, so a refactor could downgrade signal-kill/cannot-start from exit 2 to exit 1 with zero test failures (not a false-pass risk; exit 1 still blocks).
findings.resolution: fixed: added a signal-kill test and a verbose-output/maxBuffer test; made the signal-kill branch an explicit block and gave ENOBUFS its own block. The generic cannot-start (interpreter ENOENT) branch stays covered by inspection + defense-in-depth (a null status downstream still blocks); it is not portably triggerable in a test.

findings.finding: an identical-branch ternary (dead code): both the .sh and non-.sh branches built the same args array.
findings.resolution: fixed: replaced with a single array.

findings.finding: the default 1 MB maxBuffer meant a legitimately-passing but verbose checker would trip ENOBUFS and be blocked, misattributed as 'could not start' (fail-closed-safe, never a false pass).
findings.resolution: fixed: raised maxBuffer to 10 MB and gave ENOBUFS its own 'output too large' block message.

findings.finding: the inline existsSync+statSync was not wrapped like the isDir helper, so a TOCTOU removal between the checks could throw uncaught.
findings.resolution: fixed: added an isFile helper (try/catch) used for resolution, so a disappearing file blocks cleanly.

findings.finding: the contributor-process artifacts (receipt + this review log) were not yet in the change set.
findings.resolution: fixed: this review entry and the skill receipt are landed before the PR is opened; npm run check:receipt is green.
